segments.en: Hello, English learners.
segments.zh: 各位英语学习者，大家好。

segments.en: Welcome back to another lesson here at EnglishPod.
segments.zh: 欢迎回到 Englishpod 的另一个课程。

segments.en: My name is Marco.
segments.zh: 我叫 Marco。

segments.en: And my name is Catherine.
segments.zh: 我叫 Catherine。

segments.en: Hello, everyone.
segments.zh: 大家好。

segments.en: Today, Marco, what are we talking about?
segments.zh: 今天，马可，我们在说什么？

segments.en: Well, today we are not really in the best mood.
segments.zh: 好吧，今天我们的心情不是最好的。

segments.en: What do you mean?
segments.zh: 你是什么意思？

segments.en: We're kind of sad.
segments.zh: 我们有点难过。

segments.en: We're kind of nervous.
segments.zh: 我们有点紧张。

segments.en: We're not feeling very well.
segments.zh: 我们感觉不太好。

segments.en: It's a cloudy day.
segments.zh: 这是一个阴天。

segments.en: Maybe that's why.
segments.zh: 也许这就是原因。

segments.en: The blues.
segments.zh: 忧郁；情绪低落。

segments.en: The blues.
segments.zh: 忧郁；情绪低落。

segments.en: So, yeah, that's what we're talking about today.
segments.zh: 所以，是的，这就是我们今天所说的。

segments.en: We're going to have a lot of different descriptive words to express maybe feeling sad or maybe you're angry or you're nervous or something like that.
segments.zh: 我们将有很多不同的描述性词语来表达可能感到悲伤，或者你很生气，或者你很紧张或类似的事情。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: Well, this is a very useful lesson.
segments.zh: 嗯，这是一节非常有用的课。

segments.en: Hopefully, you're not feeling this way.
segments.zh: 希望你没有这种感觉。

segments.en: But if you have to talk about someone who is, I've got lots of words for you.
segments.zh: 但如果你不得不谈论一个人，我有很多话要告诉你。

segments.en: But first, we're going to preview a couple in today's vocabulary preview.
segments.zh: 但首先，我们将在今天的词汇预览中预览一些。

segments.en: Vocabulary preview.
segments.zh: 词汇预览。

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So, today on vocabulary preview, we're going to look at two words.
segments.zh: 所以，今天在词汇预览中，我们将看看两个词。

segments.en: And the first one is a way of saying that you feel sad.
segments.zh: 第一个是说你感到悲伤的一种方式。

segments.en: So, basically, I'm feeling down.
segments.zh: 所以，基本上，我情绪低落。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: Down.
segments.zh: 情绪低落；心情不好。

segments.en: You might have heard this before because it's the opposite of the word up.
segments.zh: 您可能以前听说过，因为它与 Up 的相反。

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: So, you're not feeling up happy looking up.
segments.zh: 所以，你不是感觉情绪高涨、开心。

segments.en: You're feeling down.
segments.zh: 你心情不好。

segments.en: This is another word for sad like Marco said.
segments.zh: 这是像马可所说的悲伤的另一个词。

segments.en: Or you can also say I'm a bit down today, right?
segments.zh: 或者你也可以说我今天有点沮丧，对吧？

segments.en: Yeah, I'm a bit down today.
segments.zh: 是的，我今天有点沮丧。

segments.en: Or you look really down.
segments.zh: 或者你看起来真的很低落。

segments.en: Are you okay?
segments.zh: 你还好吗？

segments.en: Yeah.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: So, you look sad.
segments.zh: 所以，你看起来很伤心。

segments.en: Are you... is everything okay?
segments.zh: 你……一切都好吗？

segments.en: So, down.
segments.zh: 所以，down 就是情绪低落。

segments.en: So, now another feeling or a way that a person is feeling, maybe that person is grouchy.
segments.zh: 所以，现在一个人的另一种感觉或一种方式，也许那个人很不高兴。

segments.en: Would you please stop talking so loud, Marco?
segments.zh: 马可，你能不能别说得那么大声？

segments.en: I think you have...
segments.zh: 我想你有...

segments.en: No, I'm seriously.
segments.zh: 不，我是认真的。

segments.en: Don't be grouchy, Kathryn.
segments.zh: 不要不高兴，凯瑟琳。

segments.en: Geez.
segments.zh: 天哪。

segments.en: No.
segments.zh: 不。

segments.en: So, grouchy is a way someone acts, usually when they're in a bad mood.
segments.zh: 所以，不高兴是一个人的行为方式，通常是在他们心情不好的时候。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: So, it's not like really angry.
segments.zh: 所以，这不像真的生气。

segments.en: You're not angry, but you're not very happy either.
segments.zh: 你不生气，但你也不是很开心。

segments.en: And you're not very nice to people.
segments.zh: 而且你对人不是很好。

segments.en: So, there's a very famous TV character called Oscar the Grouch on Sesame Street.
segments.zh: 所以，芝麻街上有一个非常著名的电视角色，叫做奥斯卡·格劳奇。

segments.en: Look for him on YouTube or Youku.
segments.zh: 在 YouTube 或 Youku 上寻找他。

segments.en: And he's very, very good for learning about this feeling, grouchy, because he's a grouchy guy.
segments.zh: 他非常非常适合了解这种感觉，不高兴，因为他是一个不高兴的人。

segments.en: Yeah, he's always angry or never happy, basically.
segments.zh: 是的，基本上，他总是生气或从不快乐。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: He's always complaining about something.
segments.zh: 他总是抱怨某事。

segments.en: So, that word again is grouchy.
segments.zh: 所以，这个词就是 grouchy，爱发牢骚。

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So, after taking a look at these two words, we're ready now to listen to our dialogue for the first time.
segments.zh: 所以，在看了这两个词之后，我们现在准备好第一次听我们的对话了。

segments.en: Let's see what this dialogue is about, if maybe they're grouchy or maybe just sad.
segments.zh: 让我们看看这个对话是关于什么的，如果它们可能很不高兴或只是悲伤。

segments.en: Fine.
segments.zh: 好。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: I'll talk to you later.
segments.zh: 回头聊。

segments.en: Bye.
segments.zh: 再见。

segments.en: Carrie, are you okay?
segments.zh: Carrie，你还好吗？

segments.en: You seem a bit down.
segments.zh: 你似乎有点沮丧。

segments.en: I just got off the phone with my boyfriend.
segments.zh: 我刚和男朋友通了电话。

segments.en: He's always getting upset and losing his temper over nothing.
segments.zh: 他总是无缘无故地生气、发脾气。

segments.en: It's so hard to talk to him at times.
segments.zh: 有时很难和他说话。

segments.en: Maybe it's just that he's stressed out from working or something.
segments.zh: 也许只是他因工作而感到压力很大。

segments.en: He does have a pretty nerve-wracking job, you know.
segments.zh: 你知道，他确实有一份相当伤脑筋的工作。

segments.en: Yeah, but he's always in a really foul mood.
segments.zh: 是的，但他总是心情很糟糕。

segments.en: I try to find out what's bothering him or get him to talk about his day, but he always shuts down and brushes me off.
segments.zh: 我想弄清楚他为什么烦心，或者让他聊聊一天过得怎么样，可他总是闭口不谈，对我不理不睬。

segments.en: Men are like that, you know.
segments.zh: 男人就是这样，你知道的。

segments.en: They can feel nervous, anxious, or on edge, and the only way they can express it is by trying to hide it through aggressiveness.
segments.zh: 他们可能感到紧张、焦虑或烦躁，却只能用咄咄逼人的态度掩饰这些情绪。

segments.en: I guess you're right.
segments.zh: 我想你说得对。

segments.en: What do you think I should do?
segments.zh: 你觉得我该怎么办？

segments.en: He wasn't always this grouchy, you know.
segments.zh: 要知道，他以前可没这么爱发牢骚。

segments.en: Talk to him.
segments.zh: 和他谈谈。

segments.en: Cheer him up when he's down, and if that doesn't work, I say get rid of him and get a new one.
segments.zh: 他情绪低落时就哄哄他；要是没用，我看你干脆甩了他，再找一个。

segments.en: You are something else, you know that?
segments.zh: 真有你的，你知道吗？

segments.en: Alright so two girls talking about guys.
segments.zh: 好吧，两个女孩在谈论男人。

segments.en: I guess guys have a bad temper sometimes, right?
segments.zh: 我想男人有时脾气不好，对吧？

segments.en: I think anyone can have a bad temper, but we're talking today about the boyfriend of one of these girls who has a very bad temper and has been very grouchy recently.
segments.zh: 我认为任何人都可能脾气暴躁，但我们今天谈论的是其中一个女孩的男朋友，他脾气很坏，最近一直很爱发牢骚。

segments.en: And that's why she's feeling a bit down.
segments.zh: 这就是为什么她感觉有点沮丧。

segments.en: So let's take a look at those words now in Language Takeaway.
segments.zh: 所以我们现在就在语言要点中看看这些词。

segments.en: Language Takeaway Alright so in today's Language Takeaway, we've got some wonderful words for you.
segments.zh: 语言要点 好吧，在今天的语言要点中，我们为您准备了一些很棒的词。

segments.en: Words that are very good for describing stress or having anxiety.
segments.zh: 非常适合描述压力或焦虑的词。

segments.en: The first of these words is something you hear all the time, especially with young people.
segments.zh: 这些词中的第一个是您一直听到的，尤其是在年轻人中。

segments.en: Right, somebody is stressed out.
segments.zh: 对，有人压力很大。

segments.en: Oh my gosh, Marco, I'm so stressed out.
segments.zh: 哦，天哪，马可，我压力很大。

segments.en: I have ten homework assignments to do and softball practice and my mom wants me to help cook dinner tonight.
segments.zh: 我有十个作业要做，还要练垒球，我妈妈还希望我今晚帮忙做晚饭。

segments.en: You really are stressed out.
segments.zh: 你真的压力很大。

segments.en: I am stressed out.
segments.zh: 我压力过大。

segments.en: I don't have any homework and I don't live with my mom.
segments.zh: 我没有作业，也没有和妈妈住在一起。

segments.en: But being stressed out is usually something you feel when you have too much stuff to do.
segments.zh: 但是当你有太多事情要做时，你通常会感到压力过大。

segments.en: So maybe you can be stressed out because of school, like in your case, or maybe at work you have a lot of things to do or a project to finish, right?
segments.zh: 所以也许你会因为学校而压力大，就像你的情况，或者在工作中你有很多事情要做，或者有个项目要完成，对吧？

segments.en: Exactly and I just want to point out here that you can say I'm stressed or I'm feeling stressed but commonly in spoken English, so when you're talking to your friends, you hear this much more often, stressed out.
segments.zh: 确切地说，我只想在这里指出，你可以说 I'm stressed 或 I'm feeling stressed，但通常在日常口语中，也就是你和朋友说话时，更常听到的是 stressed out。

segments.en: Stressed out, he's really stressed out lately.
segments.zh: 压力很大，他最近真的压力很大。

segments.en: So we're stressed out or another word that kind of means the same is this is nerve-wracking.
segments.zh: 所以我们压力很大，或者另一个意思是同样的词，这就是令人伤脑筋。

segments.en: Nerve-wracking, so nerves are those things in our body that help us feel things, right?
segments.zh: 伤脑筋，所以我们体内的神经是帮助我们感受事物的东西，对吧？

segments.en: And so something that racks our nerves makes us very, very tense, very anxious, very uncomfortable.
segments.zh: 所以让我们紧张的事情让我们非常、非常紧张、非常焦虑、非常不舒服。

segments.en: Okay, so it makes you very nervous.
segments.zh: 好吧，所以这让你很紧张。

segments.en: Right, so there are some movies that are nerve-wracking.
segments.zh: 是的，所以有些电影令人伤脑筋。

segments.en: For example, suspense movies like Hitchcock's movies like Psycho or The Birds.
segments.zh: 例如，像希区柯克的电影 Psycho 或 The Birds 这样的悬疑片。

segments.en: Like Horror, like maybe Saw.
segments.zh: 像恐怖片，比如《电锯惊魂》(Saw)。

segments.en: Nerve-wracking, also some people think that roller coasters are nerve-wracking.
segments.zh: 令人伤脑筋，也有人认为坐过山车令人紧张。

segments.en: They're very, very anxious when they ride roller coasters.
segments.zh: 他们乘坐过山车时非常非常焦虑。

segments.en: Right, so let's listen to a couple of more examples of in different situations where we can use this phrase nerve-wracking.
segments.zh: 对，我们再听几个例子，看看 nerve-wracking 这个短语还能用在哪些不同情境中。

segments.en: Example one.
segments.zh: 例句一。

segments.en: I think being a doctor is one of the most nerve-wracking jobs in the world.
segments.zh: 我认为成为一名医生是世界上最伤脑筋的工作之一。

segments.en: Example two.
segments.zh: 例句二。

segments.en: Skydiving was one of the most nerve-wracking experiences of my life.
segments.zh: 跳伞是我一生中最伤脑筋的经历之一。

segments.en: I almost had a heart attack.
segments.zh: 我差点心脏病发作。

segments.en: Example three.
segments.zh: 例句三。

segments.en: The final match between Brazil and Italy was incredibly nerve-wracking.
segments.zh: 巴西和意大利之间的最后一场比赛令人难以置信的伤脑筋。

segments.en: And there's another way to describe this feeling.
segments.zh: 还有另一种方式来描述这种感觉。

segments.en: Again, it's a little bit different but very, very similar.
segments.zh: 同样，它有点不同，但非常非常相似。

segments.en: We can say someone is feeling on edge.
segments.zh: 我们可以说有人感到紧张。

segments.en: On edge.
segments.zh: 紧张不安；烦躁。

segments.en: So this person was feeling on edge, but what does that mean exactly?
segments.zh: 所以这个人感觉很紧张，但这到底是什么意思？

segments.en: You're like at the edge?
segments.zh: 你就像在边缘？

segments.en: Why do you have to ask so many questions?
segments.zh: 为什么你要问这么多问题？

segments.en: Okay, listen.
segments.zh: 好吧，听着。

segments.en: This is basic.
segments.zh: 这是基本的。

segments.en: Okay, Marco?
segments.zh: 好吧，马可？

segments.en: All right, all right.
segments.zh: 好吧，好吧。

segments.en: Are you mocking me?
segments.zh: 你在嘲笑我吗？

segments.en: I'm on edge today.
segments.zh: 我今天很紧张。

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So someone who is on edge is easily angered, right?
segments.zh: 所以紧张不安的人很容易被激怒，对吧？

segments.en: So it's very easy to make this person upset or angry.
segments.zh: 所以很容易让这个人烦躁或生气。

segments.en: Someone who just quit smoking might be on edge.
segments.zh: 刚戒烟的人可能会烦躁不安。

segments.en: That means it's very, very easy to get them to be upset.
segments.zh: 这意味着很容易让他们心烦意乱。

segments.en: Wow.
segments.zh: 哇。

segments.en: So yeah, you are on edge, right?
segments.zh: 所以，是的，你现在很烦躁，对吧？

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: He's on edge or he seems on edge, doesn't he?
segments.zh: 他很紧张，或者他看起来很紧张，不是吗？

segments.en: Okay, very good.
segments.zh: 好，很好。

segments.en: Wow, these three words that we've just looked at are really interesting and very, very useful.
segments.zh: 哇，我们刚刚看过的这三个词真的很有趣，也非常非常有用。

segments.en: I guess you can describe many different situations or a person that's going through these feelings, right?
segments.zh: 我想你可以描述许多不同的情况或一个正在经历这些感觉的人，对吧？

segments.en: Absolutely.
segments.zh: 当然。

segments.en: I think there is a thousand ways to describe being nervous or anxious or upset.
segments.zh: 我认为有一千种方法可以描述紧张、焦虑或不安。

segments.en: So maybe we should take another listen to today's dialogue and figure out how exactly we use these words and we come back.

segments.en: Bye.
segments.zh: 再见。

segments.zh: 他们表达情绪的唯一方式，就是用咄咄逼人的态度来掩饰。

segments.zh: 我想你说得对。

segments.zh: 你觉得我该怎么办？

segments.zh: 你知道，他并不总是那么不高兴。

segments.zh: 所以，马可，这是一个大问题。

segments.en: What makes you lose your temper?
segments.zh: 是什么让你发脾气？

segments.en: I think what makes me lose my temper very, very easily is like a dirty house or like a dirty room.
segments.zh: 我认为让我很容易发脾气的是，就像一个肮脏的房子或一个肮脏的房间。

segments.en: You're a neat freak.
segments.zh: 你是个有洁癖的人。

segments.zh: 不算是洁癖，但如果房间不是至少半干净，你知道，我就会很在意。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So this great phrase, lose your temper or lose one's temper is a phrase we use in English to describe getting angry.
segments.zh: 所以这个很棒的短语 lose your temper，或者说 lose one's temper，是英语里用来形容发怒的说法。

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So maybe you're okay.
segments.zh: 所以也许你没事。

segments.en: You're frustrated with something, but someone does something like throws all of their clothes on the floor and Marco here says, that's it.
